interface.title: qPilot
interface.field: Molecular biology: relative gene-expression analysis by quantitative PCR (qPCR / RT-qPCR)
interface.stage_of_work: Data analysis after the instrument run: quality-checking raw amplification curves, normalising, testing fold change, checking robustness, reporting and export
interface.what_it_is_for: Takes raw qPCR instrument curves to per-gene fold-change calls. The analysis stays blind until a person confirms the experimental design and the amplification calls. The tool then shows which analysis choices could flip each conclusion and keeps every decision in a hash-chained, exportable record.

data.note: Built-in demo study: Vermeulen 2009 neuroblastoma RDML (data_vermeulen_raw.rdml, SHA-256 bc1d233e3866…). On opening, Design lists 66 targets and 427 samples; after the design is applied, 64 plates (24,576 reactions) are analysed and 58 genes compared across 366 samples, MYCN-high (53) vs rest (294). No AI model was configured ('no model'), so qPilot's fixed rules made every proposal; with no model these rules propose only sample roles, dilution series and gene symbols, not groups or reference genes. The test uploads (lc96_bACTXY.rdml, hmuy_cq_values.xlsx) were not tried.

tree.general: Turn raw instrument measurements into per-item group-difference calls that a person has checked, can defend and can reproduce
tree.specific: Take raw qPCR curves to per-gene fold-change calls with Decision Cards, a robustness map, plate-control checks, a Prism export and a hash-chained Analysis Record

features.name: Proposal inbox with engine check and bulk triage
features.general: Machine-made suggestions arrive as cards, each with its evidence, an independent consistency check (Consistent / Contradicted / Cannot check) and a consequence. A person accepts, edits or rejects each one with a reason, or works in bulk on all the consistent or all the contradicted ones. A preview dialog lists exactly what will be written.
features.specific: Design and Curves proposal cards (WHY, ENGINE CHECK, CONSEQUENCE, LEVEL) with Accept / Edit… / Reject…, reason chips, j/k/a/e/x keys, filters by status and kind, a search box, and 'Accept all consistent…' / 'Reject contradicted proposals…' dialogs that take one shared reason
steps: Press Propose the design or Check the curves
Filter the inbox by status or kind
Reject contradicted cards with a reason chip, singly or in bulk
Open Edit… to see the preset readings (an unchanged edit is refused)
Accept all consistent ones after checking the listed items
serves_tasks: Have rule-made proposals for sample roles, dilution series and item names checked and accept or reject each with a reason; take the groups and reference items from a stored study design (or set them by hand)
Settle the validity rule and the disputed calls, then freeze them

features.name: Blind staged confirmation gate
features.general: Results stay hidden until the input definitions are frozen in order. Each freeze opens a dialog listing exactly what it covers and its fingerprint. A later change reopens the stage.
features.specific: Design then Curves 'Confirm this stage…' dialogs (design fingerprint 2000023796a6, sample types, dilution series, gene symbols, amplification rule). Confirm stays disabled until every proposal is decided and the design has reference genes and two groups. Curves, Results, Controls, Audit, Prism and the tools show lock icons until both stages are confirmed; 'Confirm the analysis choices' then locks the choices for Prism
steps: Decide every waiting proposal
Press Confirm this stage…
Read the covered items and fingerprint
Press Yes, confirm (the next stage unlocks)
serves_tasks: Freeze the design after reviewing exactly what it covers
Lock all decided analysis choices so downstream exports use exactly them

features.name: Plate map linked to a multi-curve viewer
features.general: A well-plate grid coloured by a chosen per-well metric, with a hover tooltip. Clicking or Ctrl-clicking wells overlays their raw traces with threshold markers, a Linear/Log toggle, drag-to-zoom, a cursor readout and a per-well table.
features.specific: Curves → The plate (Gene and Plate selectors, previous/next plate, colouring by Amplification call / Cq / Efficiency / R² / Sample type, View as table). Well panel shows raw fluorescence with Cq lines and baseline, Linear/Log, and a LinRegPCR vs Curve Judge table. The selection is kept in the URL (/curves/plate/A1,P20,H2)
steps: Pick a plate and a colouring
Hover a well for its tooltip
Click a well, Ctrl-click more to compare
Switch to Log and drag across cycles to zoom; double-click resets
serves_tasks: Inspect individual measurements on a plate layout and compare their raw traces
features.evidence: unverified: its screenshots were overwritten; screens/003.webp shows only loading placeholders

features.name: Decision Card with per-option outcome preview
features.general: For each analysis choice that could change a conclusion, every option is listed with the result it would give for the headline items. Flips are marked 'changes' and options are tagged Recommended or Not recommended. The person picks one and must type a reason, which goes into the record.
features.specific: Results → Decision Cards (control-gene set, group cut-off, amplification/Cq cut-off, empty-well rule). Each shows how many of the 58 conclusions change, fold changes for BIRC5/NM23A/NTRK1/ODC1 per option, 'How this was worked out', a required 'Why this option?' and Decide (Ctrl+Enter)
steps: Open a card and press Show all options
Compare per-option fold changes and flips
Select an option
Type a reason
Press Decide or Ctrl+Enter (the card shows 'Decided by you … Reason: …')
serves_tasks: Make each conclusion-changing analysis choice, seeing what every option would do and giving a reason
features.evidence: screens/049.webp shows only decided cards on a gene page; the per-option preview has no surviving screen

features.name: Robustness map with gene drill-down
features.general: A scatter of every item's effect size against the share of all reasonable analysis combinations that keep its call, colourable by call or confidence and linked to a filterable table. Clicking an item opens its page: the distribution of results across all combinations with the planned analysis marked, and which single choices can flip it.
features.specific: Results → Robustness map (Call / Confidence / Audit verdict colourings, 2× lines, View as table) plus the All genes table (search, Up/Down/No call, confidence, 'Only genes one choice can flip'). Gene page (e.g. NM23A) shows fold change, CI, p, confidence reasons, a 744-analysis dot plot and the 'One choice at a time' cards
steps: Switch the colouring between Call and Confidence
Hover or arrow-key to read a gene
Click a gene to open its page
Read the 744-analysis distribution and which cards can change the call alone
serves_tasks: See how much each item's call depends on the analysis choices, and open one item

features.name: Control-rule gate with leave-out impact and well tracing
features.general: Control samples on every plate are checked against a versioned rule pack. Each plate shows its worst verdict. Opening a rule shows its reason and the exact wells, and the whole analysis is re-run without those wells. A Decision Card appears only where leaving them out would change a conclusion.
features.specific: Controls: plate chips (Fail / Warn / Pass), Rule checks with status tabs and a rule dropdown, 'What leaving the wells out would change' (Changes no call / Changes a call, Show the check), and 'Decision Cards from the controls' (Keep every well vs Leave out the wells this rule flags; seen, not decided)
steps: Read the one-line summary (fail/warn/pass)
Click a plate chip to see only its checks
Expand a failing rule for its reason and wells
Open 'Show the check' on a row that changes a call
serves_tasks: Review control-sample rule results per plate and see whether dropping the flagged wells changes any conclusion

features.name: Stepped export to statistics software with route comparison
features.general: A four-step stepper (lock choices → draft → send → round trip). It first shows how many conclusions the common manual route would get differently. Then it drafts a project as an acceptable proposal, previews each table and graph, and writes a downloadable bundle.
features.specific: Prism: 'What the usual route into Prism would change' (4, 14 and 21 of 58 differ). Draft the Prism project → accept the proposal → per-gene preview tabs with dot plot and CSV → Send to Prism → Download the bundle (.pzfx plus CSV plus README)
steps: Lock the analysis choices in Results
Press Draft the Prism project
Accept the drafted proposal
Preview each gene's table
Press Send to Prism and download the bundle
serves_tasks: Show how the usual spreadsheet route would change the conclusions, then produce a statistics-software project from the engine's numbers

features.name: Hash-chained decision log with export
features.general: Every human or automatic decision is a timeline entry carrying its reason, author and a hash linked to the previous entry, with an integrity badge and filtering by author. One button exports a reproducible zip; a drop zone for verifying someone else's record is also offered.
features.specific: Record: Decision chain (Head, Entries, 'Intact: every hash checks out', filters All / You / Agents / qPilot), Export the Analysis Record (record id, chain head, 16 files, input included, Download the record), 'Verify a record' drop zone (not tried), 'Check it anywhere' CLI hints. The chain stays empty until design and curves are confirmed
steps: Read the decision chain and integrity badge
Filter by author
Press Export the Analysis Record
Download the zip
serves_tasks: Review the tamper-evident decision log and export a reproducible record
